title: Develop scoping playbook for enterprise private deployment requests (networking, upgrades, air-gapped)
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable scoping playbook and decision checklist for intake of enterprise requests that involve Private / VPC / On‑prem deployments where networking constraints, OS/firmware upgrade windows, and air‑gapped requirements create non‑trivial project scope.

Background: We continue to see long tail enterprise asks that require triage across networking architecture, upgrade policies, and air‑gap constraints. These requests frequently stall in intake or bounce between SE, Eng, and Legal. The playbook should standardize questions, a scoring heuristic for prioritization, required stakeholders by score, and an expected timeline template to communicate to customers.

Goals:
- Reduce initial scoping time by 30% (time-to-first-estimate).
- Ensure consistent routing: light requests to SE, medium require Solutions + Security review, high require dedicated onboarding and Eng planning.
- Create a concise packet (one page) for Sales/SE to send to customers with clear ask checklist.

Scope (what this ticket will produce):
- Complete scoping playbook document (one‑pager + appendix).
- Prioritization scoring rubric with example weights.
- Standardized intake form template (for Zendesk/Notion/Forms).
- Stakeholder matrix mapping score bands to required reviewers and SLAs.
- Three worked example customer scenarios and suggested communication templates.

Out of scope: implementation of an automated intake system (separate follow‑up), changes to Dedicated pricing or contractual terms (will trigger separate PM work).
acceptance_criteria: One‑page scoping playbook PDF checked into PM drive
Intake form template added to Notion and linked from Sales playbook
Scoring rubric reviewed and approved by Security and Solutions Eng
Stakeholder routing matrix sign‑off from Eng Manager and Support Lead
Three sample customer scenarios with recommended routing and estimated timelines
success_metrics: 30% reduction in avg time from request to first written estimate (tracked via ticket timestamps)
>80% agreement between initial routing and final required review path (measured on 50 sample requests)
Decrease in reassignments between teams during first 14 days of the ticket by 40%
intake_form_fields: Connectivity model (outbound-only, inbound, full mesh, air‑gapped)
Preferred hardware / cloud provider / on‑prem OS
Upgrade/maintenance window constraints and policy (cadence, approvals)
Data residency and encryption needs (KMS/HSM required)
Egress/inbound firewall/IP allowlist feasibility and contact
Desired go‑live target date and hard deadlines
scoring_rubric: Network complexity (0–5): 0=standard outbound internet allowed; 5=air‑gapped with hardware isolation
Upgrade sensitivity (0–5): 0=can accept rolling upgrades; 5=no upgrades without customer approval and long vendor windows
Compliance burden (0–5): 0=none; 5=regulated (FedRAMP/ITAR) requiring audit logs and HSM
Operational support level (0–5): 0=self‑serve; 5=dedicated onboarding with 24/7 SLA
Total score interpretation: 0–6=Low (SE handle, estimate <2w), 7–12=Medium (Solutions + Security review, estimate 2–6w), 13–20=High (Eng planning, potential contract negotiation, estimate 6–12w)
stakeholders: Platform Eng (high score for on‑prem/autonomous installs)
sample_scenarios: Scenario A — Outbound‑only VPC (Low score): customer can allow outbound HTTPS to hosted endpoints, requires KMS integration. Routing: SE -> quick Security checklist -> CS. Estimated timeline: 1–2 weeks.

Scenario B — VPC with strict allowlist and quarterly upgrade freeze (Medium score): requires Solutions Eng to design NAT/EGress config, Security to validate KMS/HSM plan, and a scheduled rollout aligned with customer maintenance window. Estimated timeline: 3–6 weeks.

Scenario C — Air‑gapped on‑prem with no external connectivity (High score): requires full on‑prem package, signed air‑gap checklist, Eng capacity planning for on‑site installers or customer‑run helm charts, and legal review for licensing. Estimated timeline: 8–12 weeks; triggers Private deployment contract.
open_questions: Should we automatically surface an estimated price band based on score? (Sales asked for quick ballpark)
Where will the canonical intake form live (Zendesk vs Notion vs shared Drive form)? Ops prefers Zendesk; SE prefers Notion templates.
Do we require a mandatory Security intake for Medium score items or can Security be on request?
What is the exact SLA for Solutions Eng review when a ticket is flagged Medium? (propose 5 business days)
